trust_boundary: These certificates concern successful pure functions.

File IO, command-line parsing/status formatting and Lean runtime/native compilation remain outside the pure semantic theorems. Pure canonical WAT rendering is certified where its module/text contract is listed.
Validation/check receipts and CI status are reported separately; this inventory does not assert that full CI passed.
Export-session theorems concern named function-invocation scripts. Arbitrary embedder reads/writes of exported memory/globals between calls require a separate contextual contract.

The inventory checker validates source references, selected pure-endpoint dependency links and runtime isolation. It does not compile proofs, inspect axioms, or establish whole-CLI correctness; build the listed Lean proof roots separately.

exit_codes.4: Shell trap, exception or non-successful initialization result

output_policy: Pure processing completes before opening output; rejected input preserves existing/absent output paths. An IO write failure may occur after processing succeeds.

tools.contract: The complete accepted original Core WAT or independently specified Binaryen source-macro input and emitted bytes denote the same validated Core module. Existing Core assembly successes are preserved exactly.
scope: Original-source Core grammar certificates cover named/numeric indices, folded/flat control, implicit function and instruction signatures, parameter/multivalue blocks, recursive function/struct/array types, inline/separate imports, memory-data and bare-module abbreviations, every table operation, reference branches/branch tables, try_table/throw, SIMD constants/shuffle/lanes, and stateful declarations.

Source-directed elaboration checks exact source subtrees and its identifier/type-context fixed point; the original canonical reification API remains available. Original text is certified without trusting normalized output or the separate Rust wat parser.

The separate Binaryen macro grammar supports bare struct fields, array field wrappers and passive/declarative element segments omitting func. It preserves exact original source certification without weakening Core.ModuleT. Shared/atomic, continuation, descriptor, exact-reference and other proposal syntax, legacy exception instructions, tuple source macros and annotation payloads with nested groups/reserved punctuation remain incomplete. General WAST scripts and component-file assembly are outside this frontend.

Names require valid UTF-8; data may contain arbitrary bytes using checked hexadecimal, mnemonic and Unicode escapes. Quoted Core3 identifiers and ordinary atom/string annotation payloads are supported. Unsupported syntax and invalid modules reject; IO/native compilation remain outside pure certificates.

tools.contract: Original bytes and emitted canonical WAT denote the same retained module.
scope: The command-line dispatcher preserves every existing Core/compact-import and shared-memory success. An additive standard-memory-atomic route retains complete atomic bodies and shared memory32/64 in a distinct artifact and explicit extension binary/text relations; it never claims Core validity or concurrent execution correctness.

Checked canonical rendering covers recursive function/struct/array types, every retained module field kind and import/export kind, memory/table address types and initialization, segments, starts, plus context-aware indexed/indirect/reference/GC/SIMD/exception instruction syntax.

Decoder/renderer acceptance is incomplete. The assembler accepts a narrower source surface; disassembly does not itself prove validity or unconditional reassembly acceptance. No full upstream WAST or component-file codec parity is claimed.
No byte/custom-section/source-format preservation; retained-module round trips require both calls to succeed. IO/native compilation remain outside pure certificates.

Shared memories require an explicit maximum. The atomic route covers the complete 66-access classic linear-memory table, fence and pause, including nested control, memory64 and explicit memory indices. GC/reference atomics, wait queues and other unsupported proposal syntax still reject; explicit linear-memory ordering is handled by the subsequent memory profile. Empty compact descriptor groups retain their original-byte extension certificate; AST projection is not a converse original-byte Core grammar theorem.

A further additive Binaryen memory profile retains scalar and full-width v128 array backing with its trailing type index, and explicit seqcst/acqrel/relaxed linear-memory atomic orders. Its independent binary/text grammars do not relabel backing/order bits as Core alignments. Concurrent semantics, experimental-proposal validity, GC atomics and wait queues remain outside this codec contract.

Legacy exception syntax retains nested try/do, ordered tagged catches, final catch_all, delegate and rethrow in a distinct complete-body AST and independent original-byte/canonical-text relations. All earlier profile successes remain unchanged. Runtime IO, operational exception equivalence and validity of every decoded module are outside the codec theorem.

tools.contract: Original input meaning in Core plus the explicit compact-import grouping extension, ordinary Core output meaning and validity; arbitrary ordered selections and rounds have exact same-profile initialization/session equivalence at any host-state type under the closed host. Optional growth policies retain their separate contracts.
scope: Binary inputs; no passes by default. Ordered supported pass flags (including guarded small/leaf --inlining) and restricted -O presets, repetitions and explicit rounds.

Compact import groups are certified against a separate extension grammar and expanded with full source-module identity; standard inputs retain the original fast path. Standard-only APIs and other tool frontends retain their documented input boundaries.

Selected stages use validity-only certificates without the legacy whole-module output-profile guards or inliner type-section whitelist. Existing transforms, callee eligibility/heuristic/fuel and RUME's internal base-profile/imported-global/numeric-signature gates remain; older guarded APIs and original/experimental behavior are retained.

Presets retain version_133 feature-neutral/no-DWARF slot order, record missing slots and variant substitutions (including the small/leaf inliner for inlining-optimizing); no upstream algorithm/optimization-level parity.
Valid unsupported transformation shapes retain each pass identity fallback. Unsupported codecs/features may still reject.

Explicit --select-zero-grow-success removes an optional OOM trap only for the exact closed zero-growth wrapper, under specification-profile refinement or trap-insertion contracts; other shapes retain identity. Exact mode and competing growth policies reject before IO.
No uncertified implementation registry; --unverified rejects. IO/native compilation remain outside pure certificates.

tools.contract: Selected successful pure byte routes preserve decoded meanings and validity and prove target-to-original behavior inclusion at every same numerical profile, with explicit source namespace/export-query mapping and retained-public-name visibility for skip. Original mergeBytes successes retain their stronger exact invocation/session theorems.
scope: Closed host; arbitrary invocation argument lists after successful separate-source and target initialization.
Caller-supplied in-order acyclic function linking; distinct namespaces; equal or checked declared closed function subtypes; GC relocation guards remain.
Automatic checked finite silent starts; guarded function-only export rename/skip; exact original-byte left/right empty identities with validated import-free Core partners.

General stateful linking, declarative segments, open/cyclic imports, automatic dependency ordering, metadata/source-map/debug flags and arbitrary embedder contextual equivalence remain outside this compatible surface.

tools.contract: Successful checked byte execution certifies valid decoded meaning, completed initialization/start, named export lookup, invocation typing, actual Core steps and exact classified result.
scope: Empty initial store/import list; executable selects concrete numerical/growth choices, with the same initialization and result admitted by Profile.spec nd {} for either value of nd.

One-way specification conformance for either value of $ND with one global all-zero relaxed choice; no behavior-set equality, arbitrary nonzero relaxed-choice inclusion or exploration of all permitted outcomes.
Per-phase interpreter fuel; exhaustion is inconclusive. CLI arguments are i32 integers modulo 2^32.
General WAST/interactive/import-host execution is outside this runner.

tools.contract: Original/output byte meanings and validity; actual admission, initialization and shared-store export-session equivalence at every same numerical profile.
scope: Recognized closed i32/i64 scalar-global wrapper: serializes assignment, retains functions/exports, removes start.
Other decoded/validated modules retain exact original bytes and report skipped; malformed/invalid modules reject.
Arbitrary constructor evaluation, memory/host effects and general serialization remain unimplemented.

tools.contract: Original-source/input and output bytes denote valid modules; graph reachability selects the observed export names exactly; same-profile source-first admission/session equivalence for function-call scripts naming only those exports. Skipped output may retain unselected exports.
scope: Closed numeric-signature function-only base-profile modules; arbitrary loops/traps/direct calls.
Binaryen-shaped external graph name/reaches/root/export fields; graph imports, unknown/duplicate/dangling/absent bindings reject.

Ordinary full-export equivalence is not claimed for intentionally removed exports. Other decoded/validated module shapes retain exact original bytes and report skipped; graph parse/closure/binding errors still reject.

executables.contract_note: Old endpoint successes retain exact original observations. Compatible CLI also accepts certified original WAT and checked -S rendering; automatic checked finite silent starts; exact byte-preserving left/right empty identities with arbitrary validated import-free Core partners; checked declared function-subtype imports; checked rename/skip on bare function-only sources. The selected pure byte endpoint proves target-to-original behavior inclusion at every numerical profile with explicit namespace/query mapping and skip visibility. Unsupported metadata flags reject.
